POLICE FITNESS TEST

At a glance

The College of Policing describes a 15-metre multi-stage shuttle run. Its guidance is under review during the transition to the new public and personal safety training curriculum; confirm current requirements with the force.

What the test includes

Some programmes include more than the activities listed here.

Test protocol and standards

The College of Policing describes the 15 m multi-stage shuttle test in England and Wales. Its guidance is under review as forces move to the new public and personal safety training (PPST) curriculum. The table describes the previous administration arrangements, not a guarantee of the current standard in every force.

Scoring and scope

One length of the 15 m course is one shuttle. Level 5.4 is level five, shuttle four, not a decimal speed or a result on the 20 m test. Confirm the current policy with the force. Alternative Chester treadmill assessments may be offered by the force where a lower-limb injury prevents shuttle turns; they are not self-selected substitutes.

Before you rehearse the test

  1. Mark a true 15 m lane and use the published protocol and audio. Do not treat a 20 m beep test as a conversion.
  2. Ask your force which standard and test arrangements apply during the PPST transition. Practise controlled turns before increasing speed.

How to prepare

Independent training guidance, not official test instructions. Scale sessions to your current capacity and recover between demanding efforts.

  • Measure the lane and use the correct 15 m audio. Practise reaching the line and turning smoothly without sprinting the early levels.
  • Build aerobic capacity with easy runs or brisk walks and gradually add brief shuttle intervals.
  • Retest with the same surface, audio and footwear after adequate recovery; stop at the applicable standard or according to assessor instructions.

Putting it into a training week

Start with easy aerobic work and a small number of controlled 15 m turn repetitions. Build repeatability before doing a full test; use the same course and recording for comparisons.

Common mistakes

  • Using a 20 m beep-test recording.
  • Starting too fast, turning early, or treating the general standard as sufficient for every specialist role.

What to log

Record protocol length, final level and shuttle, surface and whether the required standard was reached.

Avoid repeated maximal tests and sudden load increases. Stop if pain, dizziness or unusual symptoms occur; use qualified supervision where appropriate.

Official test instructions

The organisation running the test is the best place to check the latest rules and requirements.

Worth knowing

  • Level 5.4 means completing four shuttles at level five at the required pace.
  • Check the standard for your actual role; do not substitute a 20 m shuttle protocol.
